description: Add MCP Stdio Transport: Create src/nexus/tools/mcp_stdio.py implementing an StdioMCPTransport class that spawns MCP servers as subprocesses and communicates via stdin/stdout JSON-RPC
steps: Create src/nexus/tools/mcp_stdio.py with class StdioMCPTransport that has the same interface as MCPClient (connect, list_tools, call_tool, disconnect) but communicates via subprocess stdio instead of HTTP.

Implement connect(command: str, args: list[str] | None = None, env: dict[str, str] | None = None) that spawns the MCP server as an asyncio subprocess with stdin=PIPE, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE. Send the JSON-RPC 'initialize' request to stdin (newline-terminated). Read and parse the response from stdout. Store server info.

Implement _send_request(method: str, params: dict) that writes a JSON-RPC message to the subprocess stdin (newline-terminated), reads the response line from stdout, and parses it. Use a monotonically increasing request ID. Include timeout handling (asyncio.wait_for on the readline).
Implement list_tools() that sends 'tools/list' JSON-RPC method and returns list[MCPTool] (reuse MCPTool from mcp_client.py).
Implement call_tool(tool_name: str, arguments: dict) that sends 'tools/call' JSON-RPC method and returns MCPResult (reuse MCPResult from mcp_client.py).
Implement disconnect() that sends a graceful shutdown signal, waits briefly, then force-kills if needed. Clean up process resources.
Add _read_stderr_task() as a background coroutine that reads stderr lines and logs them via Python logging for error diagnostics.
Add is_connected property and health_check() method (sends a ping or checks process.returncode is None).

Add comprehensive tests in tests/test_mcp_stdio.py covering: (a) connect spawns subprocess and sends initialize, (b) list_tools parses tool response, (c) call_tool sends correct JSON-RPC and parses result, (d) disconnect kills subprocess, (e) timeout handling when server is unresponsive, (f) error handling when subprocess exits unexpectedly.
acceptance_criteria: It spawns a subprocess and communicates via newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout
It implements connect(), list_tools(), call_tool(), disconnect(), is_connected, health_check()
It reuses MCPTool and MCPResult dataclasses from mcp_client.py
Timeout handling works for unresponsive servers
All new tests pass via python3.12 -m pytest tests/test_mcp_stdio.py
findings: Implementation complete with 24 tests passing. Full test suite: 1944 tests pass. Used asyncio.create_subprocess_exec mock pattern with side_effect lists for stdout responses. Note: process.wait mock needs side_effect list for disconnect force-kill scenario (first raises TimeoutError, second returns 0).
